question: Which synthetic response model, if any, predicts developer operation paths, reveal transitions, response to one randomized case-fact change and evaluator failures on held-out cases better than simple empirical, unprofiled and equally calibrated persona-prompted baselines?
inclusions: Synthetic defect-search utility and human-distribution alignment as separate targets
Human intervention-fidelity contrast as a separate target from marginal path fit
Permissioned, source-pinned developer response processes with person/case/mode splits
Neutral, untuned and calibrated persona, process-state and distribution-only comparator models
exclusions: Treating configured personas as a developer population or a measured human trait
Inferring hiring validity or fairness from synthetic response frequencies

selection_criteria: Record task, population, behavior target and split
Include positive and negative simulator findings
Separate transcript observation from inferred cognition
source_policy.conflict_handling: Report task- and case-specific disagreements; preserve rare valid human paths and reviewer uncertainty.
source_policy.freshness_rule: Recheck model, prompt, case and participant-population changes before transporting an alignment claim.

stop_conditions: Human data purpose or consent gate fails
Path taxonomy or blind coding is unreliable
Holdout or model baseline cannot be preserved
limitations: No calibrated state probabilities or consented developer path corpus
Current ten-episode canary tests one case and has a review-isolation deviation
claim_ceiling: Candidate inquiry only; no Lab admission, human alignment result or hiring inference.
